skill.name: verification-quality-assurance
skill.description: Guides code verification, truth scoring, rollback workflows, quality metrics, and CI gates for agent-assisted development.
skill.summary: Verify AI-assisted code changes with quality scores, reports, rollback guidance, and CI workflow examples.
skill.author: ruvnet

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command hits are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and example code fences. Confirmed issues remain around optional outbound metric posts, API key handling in URLs, predictable temporary files, unpinned alpha package execution, and destructive rollback guidance.

remediation.suggestion: Pin claude-flow examples to a reviewed immutable version, document trust assumptions, and avoid running registry code without user confirmation.

remediation.issue: API key passed in a monitoring URL
remediation.suggestion: Move monitoring credentials to headers or secure client configuration, and avoid exposing secrets in URLs, logs, or shell history.
Mark external posts as optional, require user-owned endpoints, and scrub reports before sending project metrics to third parties.
Use mktemp or a private temporary directory, set restrictive permissions, and delete verification reports after use.
Make dry-run and backup-first modes the default guidance, and require explicit approval before hard reset or automatic rollback.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Alpha Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill repeatedly instructs users to run npx claude-flow@alpha. That executes a mutable alpha package from the package registry and creates supply-chain code execution risk if the package changes or is compromised.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands explicitly use npx with the alpha tag across setup and workflow examples. This is a clear supply-chain execution pattern, even though the file is documentation.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Rollback Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill promotes automatic rollback workflows and includes a hard reset command. If copied into automation or run without backups, these instructions can delete local changes and damage source integrity.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file directly describes automatic rollback and shows git reset --hard HEAD~1 as a troubleshooting step. The destructive behavior is explicit and easy for automation to copy.

content.user_title: Verify Code Quality and Rollback Risk
content.value_statement: Teams need clear quality gates before AI-generated code reaches production. This skill explains verification checks, truth scores, rollback workflows, and CI reporting.
actual_capabilities: Explains truth score ranges, thresholds, trends, and quality criteria.
Describes verification checks for files, directories, tasks, and batches.
Documents rollback modes, including selective, interactive, dry-run, and backup-first workflows.
Provides CI examples for GitHub Actions and GitLab quality gates.
Covers dashboard, report, export, and monitoring workflows.
Lists troubleshooting steps and exit code meanings.
limitations: Requires Claude Flow, Git, and Node.js for the documented workflows.
Provides instructional Markdown, not a standalone verification engine.
Score accuracy depends on the external tool and project configuration.
Some examples use network exports or destructive rollback commands that need review.

use_cases.title: Check AI-Generated Changes
use_cases.description: Review generated code against correctness, security, performance, documentation, and best-practice criteria before merge.

use_cases.title: Add CI Quality Gates
use_cases.description: Use verification scores and reports to decide whether a pull request should pass automated checks.

use_cases.title: Track Agent Output Quality
use_cases.description: Compare score trends across agents, tasks, and time periods to find recurring quality issues.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Verification Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for a small change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a basic verification review for my latest code change. Summarize checks, expected score thresholds, and next actions.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a CI Quality Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a CI quality gate for pull requests. Include score thresholds, report handling, and failure behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Rollback Safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review whether automatic rollback is safe for my repository. Identify safeguards, dry-run steps, and approval points.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Quality Monitoring Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a monitoring plan for verification trends across agents and tasks. Include metrics, exports, alerts, and review cadence.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to verify one modified file before a pull request.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends a single-file verification, reviews the score threshold, checks failed criteria, and lists manual review steps before merge.

output_examples.input: A DevOps engineer wants a merge gate based on verification scores.
output_examples.output: The assistant outlines a CI gate that stores a report artifact, blocks low scores, and sends the summary to reviewers.

output_examples.input: A team wants automatic rollback after failed verification.
output_examples.output: The assistant advises dry-run testing first, backup creation, selective rollback, clear ownership, and manual approval for destructive actions.

best_practices: Review and pin external tool versions before running command examples.
Treat exported verification reports and metrics as sensitive project data.
Use dry-run and interactive rollback modes before enabling automatic rollback.
anti_patterns: Do not post verification data to third-party endpoints without approval.
Do not place API keys in URLs, logs, shell history, or process arguments.
Do not run hard reset rollback commands on work that has not been backed up.

faq.question: What does this skill help me verify?
faq.answer: It helps plan checks for correctness, security, performance, documentation, and coding practices.

faq.question: Does this skill run verification by itself?
faq.answer: No. It documents workflows that depend on Claude Flow and related local tooling.

faq.question: Can it be used with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Are rollback workflows safe by default?
faq.answer: They can be risky. Use dry-run mode, backups, and manual approval before destructive rollback.

faq.question: Can verification metrics contain sensitive data?
faq.answer: Yes. Reports may reveal project structure, quality issues, tasks, or operational details.

faq.question: What should I review before enabling CI exports?
faq.answer: Review endpoint ownership, secret handling, report contents, retention rules, and access controls.
